commits.message:
renamed presentation.html -> index.html

This is so the it can be served automatically by web servers.
initial commit

geometry: s/self.__class__/type(self)/

I believe the latter is more idiomatic Python.

tests: fix test.sh script

Now that the tests have been moved to their own modules/package, the
test.sh script no longer works.  This changeset fixes the test script to
work with the new test layout.
tests: fix copy/paste error
README: fix code snippet for cloning the repo
REAMDME.md: add reference to second talk

add a .gitignore file

To ignore some come commonly-ignored files/dirs.

circle: refactor inside() and intersects()

These methods compute the distance between two points.  The Point class
already have a .distance() method.  Let's use that!

geometry: move tests into their own module

Clean up the geometry.py module by removing the tests and putting them in
a seperate module (in a tests directory)

circle: move tests into their own module

Clean up the circle.py module by removing the tests and putting them in
a seperate module (in a tests directory)

index.html: add part two of our talk

Part II is a more in-depth talk about unit testing in Python.
Initial commit

tests: linting

Disable duplicate-code warning.
pdm: update dependencies
tests: linting

io: use str.removeprefix instead of check & assign

Small refactor.
pdm: update dependencies

plugins: add "pid" plugin

This plugin will write larry's pid to the file given by the config (or
~/.larry.pid by default)
pdm: update dependencies
cli: move data types into their own module

filters: list_filters: default to "none"

Default to "none" when there is no filter config.

cli: remove parse_args function

It's a relatively small, unneeded function.

cli: rearrange functions

higher level goes at the top.
names: silence a pylint warning

cli: simplify the interface

- __main__: use asyncio.run instead of accessing the event loop directly
- parse_args: only parse the args
- remove async_main function and add logic to run_every()
- create main() function as the (async) main function
- use asyncio.get_running_loop instead of asyncio.get_event_loop in
  async funcs

filters: new filter: sine

Take the original colors' hue to calculate the sine (or optionally
cosine or optionally both) which is used as a ratio (0-1) to amplify the
original color by.

gradient: do color arithmetic for each channel

Instead of multiplying the color by a number and then adding another
number, do the multipication and addition on the channel. This is
slightly more precise. Visually it makes little to no difference but
does have an impact when comparing colors.

Color.gradient: calculate gradient color based on distance.

Calculate color based on it's distance from the two stops. This
implementation also support multi-color gradients, though there isn't a
method on Color to expose this yet.

color: fix __add__ and __sub__ methods.

__add__ just never worked. The green and blue channels were flipped.
This goes to show I never really used it. The tests were simply wrong.

__sub__ also didn't work. Not only did it call the broken __add__ which
made it not work but it also didn't handle Color - Color the way I
(think I) intended. This method is being used by the subtract filter
however the results came out *almost* correct and so went unnoticed.
pdm: update dependencies

Color.dominant: set multiprocessing start method to "fork"

This resolves the issue with Python 3.14 not being able to pickle
locals. See https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/126831

Color.dominant: use function instead of lambda

Python 3.14 seems to not be able to pickle the lambda.

Color.dominant: run kmeans.fit() in a subprocess

This is to get around scikit-learn's joblib interfering with larry's
thread pool.

Also fallback to Color.generate_from if dominant doesn't return in time.
tests: linting

cli: exit the loop on --list-plugins and --list-filters

The previously committed resolution didn't quite pan out. This change
splits main into two: an async and non-async. The non-async is run first
and, if it is to continue running the async_main in the loop, returns
the arguments, which are passed to async_main. Otherwise None is
returned.

cli: exit the loop on --list-plugins and --list-filters

Otherwise it loops forever.

plugins: linting

Disable broad exception warning from pylint. We intentially catch (and
log) all Exceptions.

tests: plugins: ignore unused argument

Sometimes the fixture argument is not used

command: use the thread pool

Instead of using asyncio directly, which seems to be having issues when
I run it at my desktop's autostart.

plugins: do_plugin: capture and log plugin exceptions

When running a plugin causes an exception, capture and log it.

cli: default to the none filter

After years of being gradient, this no longer seems like an obvious
default. So we finally switch to "none".
filters.none: fix docstring

cli: don't pass coroutine to add_signal_handler

It needs to be a non-coroutine.
filters.vibrance: clamp the new saturation value

colors: dominant: convert colors to np.array

Possible performance tweak.
pdm: update dependencies
plugins.gtk: use the universal thread pool
pool: add type hints

plugins: use the thread pool

Use pool.run to run non-async I/O-bound tasks.

add a "universal" thread pool

The purpose of this is so that we can run non-async IO-bound code
asynchronously.  A convenience coroutine, pool.run, accepts a non-async
function (and arguments) and executes it in the thread pool.

pulgins: convert plugins to async functions

With this change plugins are converted to coroutines. This means that
plugins are called asynchronously as well as they can call
asynchronous functions.

For backwards compatibility we still run non-async plugins but issue a
warning.
vim: use dominant instead of generate_from

vim: add option to not filter background colors

Users may want to, e.g. pastelize the foreground colors but not the
background colors.

filters.hueshift: switch to random.uniform

Switch to random.uniform from random.random for a more even
distribution.

filters.hueshift: allow specifing "random" as an amount

When this is given the amount will be picked randomly.
tests: move hueshift tests into its own module

utils: remove deprecated clip function

I've determined that no more (of my) plugins use it.

utils: rename clip => clamp

TIL the difference between "clipping" and "clamping".  This function is
actually clamping. clip() will raise a DeprecationWarning. It will be
removed when I'm sure everything else has migrated.
filters: move parse_range from timeofday to utils
tests: add tests for filters.timeofday.parse_range
tests: move timeofday tests to their own module
tests: add tests for sepia.blend

config: remove the DEFAULT section

I did not like this part of ConfigParser, so I'm going to stop using it.
linting

color: remove `random` kwarg from dominant

This seems like pointless option. Callers can just call random.shuffle
on the returned list if desired.

filters.sepia: allow "random" option for coefficients

When overriding the default coefficients (via the config), allow the
value "random" to be specified, in which case a random value [0, 1) will
be used.

Also place the sepia tests in their own module as a beginning of a
refactor to start splitting filters tests into their own modules.

new filter: luminize

Changes the luminocity of colors

new filter: intensify

This calls Color.intensify() on the colors in the list.  The neonize
filter works similarly but takes absolute amounts for S and V values
whereas this filter only works on S values and takes percentages instead
of absolute values.
plugins.gnome_shell: use apply_plugin_filter
plugins.cal: use apply_plugin_filter
plugins.background: use apply_plugin_filter
fix a docstring

plugins.vim: refactor get_new_colors

So we can pass the entire list of colors to apply_plugin_filter instead
of one at a time.

vim: replace "soften" logic with apply_plugin_filter

This is not the best way of doing it but it will be better in the next
iteration. We'll basically want to rewrite how get_new_colors works.

plugins: vim: get_new_colors: pass the entire config

We're getting ready to migrate to apply_plugin_filters.

filters.timeofday: make start hours configurable

Allow the start hours for each time of day to be configurable through
the filter's config. For example the itch I'm trying to scratch here is
that I want the MORNING for my server LEDs to start at 5 AM instead of
6.

plugins: remove the filtered decorator

The filtered decorator was intended to work similarly to what
`apply_filter_plugin` does now, but it applied to the plugin itself and
the plugin only sees the filtered colors. In reality it didn't make
sense which is the reason why it was never used. This change removes the
decorator and its helper function.

plugins: add plugin helper to apply filters

Some plugins may opt to apply filters to the colors from the plugin's
config. This change makes that possible. The command plugin now adds
this ability. Others will follow.

utils: bring int-returning clip() back

This was reverted because it broke tests for larry-rgb. However other
changes break the tests too (numpy for RasterImage). We'll instead fix
the tests in larry-rgb.

filters.sepia: call int() on components

I was wrong about the reverted utils.clip change not affecting anything.
Fixed.

Revert "utils.clip: ensure returned values are integers"

The change breaks tests (but not functionality) for plugins and it
otherwise isn't used anymore. Therefore revert to original behavior.

This reverts commit e770a4de12d1ca86afdce4432174fc069e94621c.

new filter: timeofday

Adjusts brightness according to the time of day

tests: enhance AllFiltersTests

Ensure the result is a list of colors that have the same length as the
input list.
image: use numpy to get RasterImage colors
filters.colorbalance: use numpy
color.Color.distance: use scipy.spatial
color.Color: add ability to convert to/from np.arrays

new filter: sepia

Apply a sepia effect to the colors.
utils.clip: ensure returned values are integers

new filter: kaleidoscope

Every other color plus the same list reversed.

new filter: neonize

Takes the import colors and creates a "neon" effect.
filters.vga: use a list comprehension

new filter: colorbalance

Adjust the colors to achieve a more harmonious color scheme.

new filter: hueshift

Shift the hues of each color by a given amount

new filter: vibrance

From the docstring:

Given a threshold value, and for colors below this threshold, increase
saturation by a percentage of the difference between the threshold and
the original saturation.

tests: add test that applies all filters

Filters are applied with an "empty" config. This found some bugs that
are fixed.

Also the utils.new_image_colors function signature had to be changed.

tests: use a global variable

Instead of instantiating the same ColorList multiple times.
io: remove useless local variable
color: linting
